what_it_does: Large language models (AI systems that generate text) produce intermediate values during computation that are mostly small and predictable, but occasionally contain a few extremely large numbers called activation outliers. When you try to use fewer bits to represent each number (a process called quantization — rounding values to a coarser scale so they fit in less memory and run faster), these outliers force the scale to be so wide that the small values lose precision, hurting output quality. OutlierCIM is a hardware accelerator design that runs the AI model's math directly inside the memory chip (Computing-in-Memory, or CIM — the chip stores weights and also performs the multiply-and-add operations, avoiding energy-expensive data movement to a separate processor). It tackles the outlier problem with three ideas: grouping the outlier-heavy portions of each computation into dedicated tiles that are handled separately; building reconfigurable memory arrays that can represent numbers at two different precisions depending on what the data needs; and adding a small dedicated unit that handles the mixed arithmetic that arises when most numbers are stored as integers but outliers require floating-point representation. The combination aims to keep quantization accuracy high while still achieving the speed and energy benefits of in-memory computing.
